name: Static or zero IV supplied to CBC/CTR cipher (IvParameterSpec)
attack_scenario: With a fixed IV, encrypting the same plaintext prefix always yields the same ciphertext prefix, so an attacker performing a chosen/known-plaintext or dictionary attack can detect repeated login tokens or fields, and in CTR/GCM a reused IV+key leaks the keystream, enabling plaintext recovery by XORing two ciphertexts.
negative_test_hint: encrypt the same plaintext twice using a constant IV like "new IvParameterSpec(new byte[16])" and assert the code refuses a fixed IV so the two ciphertexts differ

exemplar.explanation: CWE-329 (Generation of Predictable IV with CBC Mode) and BSI TR-02102-1 require a fresh, unpredictable IV per encryption; Egele et al. 'An Empirical Study of Cryptographic Misuse in Android Applications' (ACM CCS 2013) found constant IVs to be one of the most common crypto-API misuses. A zero IV (new IvParameterSpec(new byte[16])) or an IV derived from a constant String literal makes CBC/CTR deterministic; filling the IV from SecureRandom before every encryption restores semantic security.
